structural_change: KV-GRP2 10-19 structural redesign of the KV landing group (successor of sq1/sq2/sq3): Stage 1 private ABI (no tok/tep aliases, scalar EST; H no o_dn), registered faces with kept per-leaf copies, per-domain 2-stage reset landing with kept per-leaf copies, landing rows on the 0.192-um contact-pitch build of the same SRAM (5.09 /um), LD delay ring, DOMSPLIT PC faces; floorplan two macro columns (78-um channel) + full-width upper band; clock symmetric centre-fed insertion-aware spine on ck and hck, no tree padding, safe balance, 16-sink leaves. KV-GRP3 (s2 gate review): every s2 variant FAILED textbook.reset_landing (rst_n reached 13 flops, hrst_n 8: the per-leaf copies were cleared by the port) and grp_s2c had reg->out -133 ps on o_ctl[32] (i_up landed at the S face drove the N-face pin across the tile in one cycle).  s3: the port clears only the first landing stage (copies cleared by the landed stage, D = 1, same release edge), o_ctl / o_dn leave exit face flops (+1 core edge each, priced, KV-GEN9 inbox). KV-GRP6 s6 (Codex s5 storage audit c1e5bec49): the 1024-b response payload passed four unchanged flop captures (PC out e0 -> hop e1 -> idata e2 -> exit e3; the middle three a >= 3-deep delay line, SAFE 5).  s6: per PC branch the payload delay is a genuine SRAM ring (8 x 4x32 1R1W macros, write slot wp at e1, read the previous slot at e2, exit copies at e3; unreset self-phasing pointers, read != write slot), payload cleared exactly as the old hop cleared it; metadata keeps its hop; two kept exit copies on both tiles; +0 cycles.
